question.text: An issuer with a net worth of Rs. 800 crore wants to raise funds through a QIP. What is the maximum amount it can raise?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under SEBI ICDR, the aggregate amount raised by an issuer through a Qualified Institutional Placement in a single financial year cannot exceed five times the net worth of the issuer as per its last audited financial statements. Applying that 5x cap to a net worth of Rs. 800 crore yields a maximum QIP size of 5 × Rs. 800 crore = Rs. 4,000 crore. The Trap: Rs. 2,400 crore (3x net worth) and Rs. 8,000 crore (10x net worth) apply incorrect multipliers. Rs. 1,600 crore (2x) is also too restrictive. The multiplier specifically prescribed by the QIP framework is five times the issuer's net worth. Note: The pages cited in the NISM-Series-IX Merchant Banking workbook define QIP and cover QIP conditions, pricing, monitoring, minimum allottees and resale restrictions, but do not state the 5x issuer-net-worth cap on the amount raised. The framing above is general SEBI ICDR knowledge for QIP capacity.
